He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] before declaring for the [[2011 NBA draft]] where he was drafted 19th overall by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] and then traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Harris has also played for the [[Orlando Magic]], [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Harris' career earnings are the most of any player in NBA history without an [[List of NBA All-Stars|All-Star appearance]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/tobias-harris-eclipses-300m-in-career-earnings-after-reportedly-agreeing-to-two-year-deal-with-pistons|title=Tobias Harris eclipses $300M in career earnings after reportedly agreeing to two-year deal with Pistons|last=Wimbish|first=Jasmyn|date=July 1, 2024|work=CBS Sports}} ==High school career== Harris attended [[Half Hollow Hills High School West]] and joined the varsity basketball team as an eighth grader. He played at Half Hollow Hills West until 2008 when he transferred to [[Long Island Lutheran Middle and High School]] in [[Brookville, New York]] for his junior year. He then transferred back to Half Hollow Hills West for his senior year and went on to earn the 2010 [[Mr. New York Basketball]] award. He was also named a [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web|title=Tobias Harris Bio|url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harris_tobias00.html|access-date=May 9, 2011|work=UTSports.com|archive-date=October 21, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111021022527/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harris_tobias00.html|url-status=dead}} Harris played 66 total games at Half Hollow Hills High School and averaged 24.9 points per game, 2.0 assists per game and 9.9 rebounds per game. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Tobias Harris | position = [[Forward (basketball)|F]] | hometown = [[Dix Hills, NY]] | highschool = [[Half Hollow Hills Central School District|Half Hollow Hills West HS]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = September 16, 2009 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} |- | colspan="7" style="padding-left:10px;" | '''Overall recruiting rankings:''' [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]: No. 7, [[Scout.com|Scout]]: No. 4, [[ESPN]]: No. 6 |} ==College career== Harris played for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] as a freshman in 2010–11 for coach [[Bruce Pearl]]. He played the point forward position, a mix between [[Basketball positions|forward]] and [[point guard]], in Pearl's offense. A USBWA Freshman All-America second-team selection and one of the nation's most consistent and versatile performers, Harris also was named second-team All-SEC by the league's head coaches and earned a spot on the SEC All-Freshman Team. He ranked fifth among all freshmen in the six major conferences with 15.3 points per game. In addition, his 7.3 rebounds per game ranked sixth among all major-conference freshmen. On May 9, 2011, Harris declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|title=HARRIS, HOPSON DECLARE FOR NBA DRAFT|url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050911aaa.html|access-date=May 9, 2011|work=UTSports.com|date=May 9, 2011|archive-date=May 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160524074553/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050911aaa.html|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2011–2013)=== On June 23, 2011, Harris was selected with the 19th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. He was later traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on draft night.{{cite web|first=Frank|last=Madden|url=http://www.brewhoop.com/2011/6/24/2240973/nba-draft-2011-big-trade-tobias-harris-and-jon-leuer-highlight|title=NBA Draft 2011: Big trade, Tobias Harris and Jon Leuer highlight Milwaukee Bucks' busy draft day|work=BrewHoop.com|date=June 24, 2011|access-date=June 24, 2011}} On December 10, 2011, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Bucks.{{cite web|first=Charles F.|last=Garner|title=Bucks match offer for Mbah a Moute|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/bucks/bucks-match-offer-from-denver-and-retain-free-agent-luc-richard-mbah-a-moute-ka3clla-135389088.html|access-date=December 10, 2011|work=JSOnline.com|date=December 10, 2011}} Harris made his NBA debut on January 7, 2012, against the Los Angeles Clippers before tallying a team-high 15 points a night later against the Phoenix Suns on January 8. He appeared in 42 games during his rookie season (nine starts), averaging 5.0 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 11.4 minutes per game. On October 24, 2012, the Bucks exercised their third-year team option on Harris's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2013–14 season.{{cite web |date=October 24, 2012 |title=Bucks Exercise Contract Options on Harris, Sanders and Udoh |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-exercise-contract-options-harris-sanders-and-udoh |access-date=November 17, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Orlando Magic (2013–2016)=== [[File:Tobias Harris Magic.jpg|thumb|Harris in December 2013]] On February 21, 2013, Harris was traded, along with [[Doron Lamb]] and [[Beno Udrih]], to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[JJ Redick]], [[Gustavo Ayón]] and [[Ish Smith]].{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=February 21, 2013 |title=Denton: Magic Complete Mega Trade Involving Redick; Gather More Financial Flexibility |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/denton-magic-complete-mega-trade-involving-redick-gather-more-financial-flexibility |access-date=November 17, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} Harris's playing time saw a notable increase in Orlando, and his stats followed suit. Harris more than tripled his points per game average, and more than quadrupled his rebounds, assists and blocks per game. On October 26, 2013, the Magic exercised their fourth-year team option on Harris's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2014–15 season.{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=October 26, 2013 |title=Magic Exercise Contract Options on Harkless, Harris, Nicholson and Vucevic |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-exercise-contract-options-harkless-harris-nicholson-and-vucevic |access-date=December 21, 2014 |work=NBA.com}} On January 24, 2014, Harris recorded 28 points game-winning dunk at the buzzer against Oklahoma City in what has been called one of the most exciting finishes in Orlando Magic history.{{cite news|title=Orlando Magic History 76ers]].{{cite news|title=Notebook: Magic 92, 76ers 81|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140302/PHIORL/gameinfo.html|access-date=March 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|first=Dick|last=Scanlon|date=March 2, 2014}} On Harris was born in [[Islip, New York]], to parents Lisa and Torrel, along with his five siblings. His father, Torrel, played college basketball at [[Duquesne University|Duquesne]] and [[Murray State University|Murray State]].{{Cite web|title=Tobias Harris – Men's Basketball|url=https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tobias-harris/652|access-date=February 9, 2022|website=University of Tennessee Athletics|language=en}} Former NBA player and teammate [[Channing Frye]] is Harris's first cousin.{{cite web |first=Vince |last=Ellis |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/04/15/detroit-pistons-tobias-harris-channing-frye-cleveland-cavaliers-cousins/83067180/ |title=Tobias Harris, Channing Frye having family reunion in playoffs |work=freep.com |date=April 15, 2016 |access-date=December 23, 2016}}{{cite web |first=David |last=Mayo |url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2016/04/cousins_tobias_harris_of_pisto.html |title=Cousins Tobias Harris of Pistons, Channing Frye of Cavs square off in playoffs |work=MLive.com |date=April 15, 2016 |access-date=December 23, 2016}} His grandfather, John Mulzac, was a member of the [[Tuskegee Airmen]].{{cite news |last=Stepansky |first=Joseph |last2=Bult |first2=Laura |name-list-style=and |date=February 6, 2015 |title=FDNY Lt. John Mulzac, member of Tuskegee Airmen, dies at 91 |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2015/02/06/fdny-lt-john-mulzac-member-of-tuskegee-airmen-dies-at-91/ |access-date=November 17, 2024 |newspaper=The New York Daily News}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/harris-frye-mourning-loss-grandfather/ |title=Harris, Frye Mourning Loss of Grandfather |work=NBA.com |date=January 30, 2015 |access-date=November 26, 2016 }} Harris is close friends with former NBA center [[Boban Marjanović]], who was his teammate in Detroit, Los Angeles and Philadelphia from 2016 to 2019.{{Cite web |date=August 8, 2022 |title=Tobias Harris makes hilarious clarification prior to his wedding |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/tobias-harris-makes-hilarious-clarification-prior-to-his-wedding/251385 |access-date=November 1, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}} ===Philanthropy=== Harris was the recipient of the 2016 and 2021 [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] Community Service Award. He created the "Tobias Harris School of Mentoring Program" and partnered with the [["Yes We Can" Community Center|Yes We Can Community Center]] and UAS Inc to help athletes and their parents with the recruiting and scholarship process. Harris also donated $10,000 to "Feeding Children Everywhere", a social charity that helps prepare food for hungry children.{{Cite web |last=Hawkins |first=James |date=November 16, 2016 |title=Tobias Harris wins NBA community service award |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2016/11/16/tobias-harris-wins-nba-community-service-award/93977456/ |access-date=September 25, 2022 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}} Harris launched the Tobias Lit Labs campaign which brings books and authors to families and schools. He also partnered with Read by 4th to have a block party in North Philadelphia. Harris contributed more than $2 million through his Tobias Harris Charitable Fund, which provides classroom supplies and supports professional development for educators and students. He has donated $10,000 to the [[Kappa Alpha Psi]] Foundation to provide grants for scholarships, community projects and after-school programs.{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2021 |title=Tobias Harris Receives October NBA Cares Community Assist Award |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-tobias-harris-receives-october-nba-cares-community-assist-award |access-date=September 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} Harris has also donated another $1 million to nine different charities to the Philadelphia area.{{Cite web |last=Dowd |first=Cooper |date=May 10, 2021 |title=How NBA Player Tobias Harris Reflects Christ On and Off the Court |url=https://www.movieguide.org/news-articles/how-nba-player-tobias-harris-reflects-christ-on-and-off-the-court.html |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=Movieguide {{!}} The Family Guide to Movies & Entertainment |language=en-US}} ===Spirituality=== Harris identifies as a [[Christianity|Christian]] and discusses his faith in public often.{{cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |date=May 24, 2021 |title=76ers' Tobias Harris scores playoff career-high 37 as he seeks to model life after Christ |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2021/05/24/76ers-tobias-harris-playoffs-model-life-after-christ/ |access-date=May 29, 2021 |website=Sports Spectrum}} In 2015 in an interview with "Razz and Jazz Sports", he stated, "Any person I meet, I try to embrace them and show them love so that they know I'm a Christian, Jesus Christ was a loving man. And as Christians, we have to try to model our lives after Jesus Christ".{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} ===Endorsements=== Harris has many off-court endorsements including Nike, Off-White Damari Savile, Ovadia & Sons, and more. ==References== {{Reflist|2}}{{Cite web |title=Tobias Harris' High School Basketball Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/tobias-harris/pnWcXfTsEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/basketball/stats.htm |access-date=September 15, 2022 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}} ==External links== {{commons category}} {{basketballstats|nba=202699|bbr=h/harrito02}} {{San Antonio Spurs current roster}} {{2011 NBA draft}} {{Portal bar|Sports}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Harris, Tobias}} [[Category:1992 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Suffolk County, New York]] [[Category:Charlotte Bobcats draft picks]] [[Category:Detroit Pistons players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Clippers players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Milwaukee Bucks players]] [[Category:Orlando Magic players]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:People from Dix Hills, New York]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Islip, New York]] [[Category:Philadelphia 76ers players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Huntington, New York]] [[Category:Tennessee Volunteers basketball players]]
